purpose: documents a method and the bounds the Finnish carrier evidence supports for F_i and alpha_i. it is not a table of agent values and contains none
not_produced_here: per-agent F_i, alpha_i, beta_i or fuel-surcharge values for any of the twelve logistics agents; that is v5 synthesis work
model: base_transport_cost_eur_i(t) = [F_i + alpha_i x weight_kg + beta_i x (weight_kg / 1000) x distance_km] x [1 + fuel_surcharge_i(t)], docs/data_synthesis_methodology.md section 7.1

normalization.vat: Posti parcel, Posti Express Freight and Matkahuolto Lavarahti all state prices without VAT, so they compare directly. PostNord's VAT status could not be read (HTTP 403); its figures are compared only with that flag attached
normalization.fuel_surcharge: both upper-bound sources state the fuel surcharge is charged separately, so their readings are ex-fuel, which is the shape the parametric model needs because it applies fuel_surcharge_i(t) on top. the Posti digital parcel list does not mention fuel and PostNord could not be read. no adjustment is applied, because applying one would assume an inclusion the sources do not state. the consequence is recorded instead: if either parcel tariff did include fuel, its ex-fuel F and alpha would be lower than read here, by up to Posti's 21.10% parcel surcharge of September 2026 for that source
normalization.pickup: the parcel lists price hand-in at an outlet, the Posti freight list prices outlet to recipient with pickup extra, and Lavarahti prices terminal to recipient with mandatory pickup extra. freight readings are therefore shown with and without pickup, and parcel readings are hand-in only
normalization.dates: effective dates differ: Lavarahti from 1.11.2024, the Posti freight list from 16.11.2025, the Posti parcel list 'until further notice' (file 202501), PostNord unverified. no price-level adjustment between those dates is applied

posti_express_freight.translation_method: the tariff is a price per transport unit per zone. two honest readings are given per zone: each unit price as a fixed charge valid up to that unit's gross weight limit, and a straight line through two consecutive unit types placed at their gross weight limits, whose slope is an alpha-equivalent and whose intercept is an F-equivalent. placing each price at the unit's maximum weight gives the lowest per-kg reading the unit allows; a lighter load pays the same price
posti_express_freight.capacity_assumption: the half pallet column is headed 'Rolltainer/Half pallet'; the half pallet limit of 500 kg is used, a rolltainer's limit is 250 kg, which would roughly double that column's per-kg reading
posti_express_freight.zone_caveat: zones 0-5 are not defined in the price list (the zone list is a link), so they cannot be mapped to km. prices rise with zone, which suggests zones carry distance, and only zone 0 is used as the least-distance F/alpha reading; zones 1-5 are kept to show that entanglement

matkahuolto_lavarahti.translation_method: the tariff is a price per weight bracket per distance band. only the shortest band, 1-49 km, is read for F and alpha, because every longer band adds distance cost that beta_i already represents. each bracket price is placed at its bracket midpoint and a straight line is drawn between two brackets that span the simulation's shipment weights; the slope is the alpha-equivalent and the intercept the F-equivalent. two low brackets are shown so the sensitivity to that choice is visible
matkahuolto_lavarahti.pickup_normalization: pickup is always part of the service but priced separately, so every secant is given both as published and with the pickup fee for each bracket's upper weight added

matkahuolto_lavarahti.discrete_points_note: brackets up to the service's 3000 kg shipment limit; the table itself continues to 14999 kg

supported_readings.these_are_discrete_readings: min and max are the smallest and largest readings actually computed from the evidence, not ends of a fitted or interpolated distribution

finding_on_bound_direction: the evidence supports parcel tariffs as the lower bound for F but not for alpha. parcel tariffs carry the lowest fixed charge and the highest per-kg charge (0.30 EUR/kg), while freight tariffs carry higher fixed charges and per-kg readings of about 0.048 to 0.128 EUR/kg, because freight prices capacity by the unit rather than by the kilogram. the evidence therefore describes two corners, low-F and high-alpha parcel against high-F and low-alpha freight, rather than one range in which both coefficients rise together

crossovers.freight_reading: Posti Express Freight zone 0, half pallet to pallet secant
Lavarahti 1-49 km, 100-149 to 950-999 kg secant, pickup included

parcel_freight_crossover.note: both crossovers lie above the 35 kg parcel limit, so the parcel line is not actually available at the weight where freight becomes the cheaper reading

gaps: PostNord's tariff metadata could not be read (HTTP 403, no archive capture), and its single weight bracket per zone cannot separate F from alpha
Posti's delivery zones 0-5 are not defined in the price list, so they cannot be mapped to km
the parcel evidence stops at 25 kg (35 kg oversized); the simulation's shipments are mostly far heavier, see simulation_shipment_weights
between 35 kg and a half pallet only Lavarahti's lowest brackets give evidence; there is no parcel-style F + alpha tariff for that range
whether either parcel tariff includes fuel is not stated or could not be read
the sources' effective dates span November 2024 to November 2025 and no price-level adjustment between them is applied

simulation_shipment_weights.definition: quantity x finished_weight_kg_per_unit, as the supervisor computes shipment_weight_kg
